rationale: C21 is an unmistakable drafting template for the child. The child repeats C21's three-recital structure nearly verbatim: the December 16, 1950 national-emergency recital, the same statutory description of the eight-hour limitation, and the finding of an extraordinary emergency as to public work performed by a named agency. The principal adaptation is replacing the Department of Defense with the Atomic Energy Commission and specifying that its work is essential to national defense. C24 uses substantially the same machinery and language but adds a separate defense-program recital, making it a slightly less exact model. C01 applies the same statute and emergency finding but has materially different factual recitals and predates the shared national-emergency formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 16, 1950, the President proclaimed the existence of a national emergency, which requires that the military, naval, air, and civilian defenses of this country be strengthened as speedily as possible
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 16, 1950, I proclaimed the existence of a national emergency, which requires that the military, naval, air, and civilian defenses of this country be strengthened as speedily as possible
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim opening recital, with only the speaker reference changed from “I” to “the President.”

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS by section 1 of the act of August 1, 1892, 27 Stat. 340, as amended by the act of March 3, 1913, 37 Stat. 726 (40 U.S.C. 321), the service or employment of all laborers and mechanics employed by the Government of the United States upon any public work of the United States is limited to eight hours in any one calendar day, except in case of extraordinary emergency
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS by section 1 of the act of August 1, 1892, 27 Stat. 340, as amended by the act of March 3, 1913, 37 Stat. 726 (40 U.S.C. 321), the service or employment of all laborers and mechanics employed by the Government of the United States upon any public work of the United States is limited to eight hours in any one calendar day, except in case of extraordinary emergency
shared_material.explanation: The statutory recital is reproduced verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS I find that as to public work essential to the national defense being performed by the Atomic Energy Commission an extraordinary emergency exists
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS I find that as to public work being performed by the Department of Defense an extraordinary emergency exists
shared_material.explanation: The same operative emergency finding is adapted to a different agency, with an added national-defense qualifier.
